pool_note: recall@K in bm25_recall.json / semantic_recall.json measures candidate generation over the whole corpus; AUC/MRR/nDCG here measure ranking within the supplied candidate list. Different questions.
ranked_pool: the impression's own candidate_ids, not the corpus
slice_note: article_head/article_tail use TEST-period popularity (q3_plan D8) and are analysis descriptors, never model inputs -- every number was computed before the slice existed, and no score, ranking or feature sees them.
tie_break: bm25 or cosine score, then training-period popularity, then article_id
training_period_head_tail_warning: article_head_train/article_tail_train are the Q4.5-compliant cut, computed from training-period clicks only. MEASURED, THEY ARE DEGENERATE: the head bucket holds 8-9 of 2,000 impressions (0.4%) against 99.6% in the tail, because news is fresh and test-period articles were mostly never clicked during training. Every figure in those two slices carries a ci_warning and must not be read as a head-versus-tail comparison -- MIND's article_head_train AUC of 0.85 is computed over 8 impressions. They are reported because Q4.5 requires a training-period cut, and labelled unreliable because that is what the data shows.
